BOOYSEN EXCLUSIVE

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
General Mayor Booysen, suspended head of the KZN HAWKS and alleged boss behind the Cato Manor Death Squad speaks out for the first time in his first television interview.

Unique Selling Point:
WE EXCLUSIVELY GET THE FIRST SIT DOWN INTERVIEW WITH MAJOR GENERAL JOHAN BOOYSEN!

In the four years since his suspension - he has not granted any interviews.

Summary:
In December 2011, 28 members of the Cato Manor Organised Crime Unit were arrested and accused of operating like death-squad - eight months later Major General Johan Booysen was also suspended and tipped as the man allegedly behind the unit's alleged killing spree.

We sit down and get the full story from Major General Booysen.

Further information:
Suspended KZN HAWKS Boss, Major General Johan Booysen, has had racketeering charges re-instated against him, he has beaten the NPA in court 6 times previously - he has won all the cases with costs – that means it has cost the State in excess of R2 million to take him on and lose. Further more they have spent an additional R1.7 million rand on a disciplinary hearing against Booysen – where the independent external Senior Advocate Cassim also found in favour of Booysen.

After winning all his cases, Booysen was offered a golden handsake to retire by Phiyega – I have the specifics details – he declined the offer and chose to take up his position after being cleared yet again only to be charged again.

While on suspension the HAWKS have permanently appointed a new KZN HAWKS Boss – the police are essentially paying two salaries for the job at the moment.

For the first time in a sit down interview Booysen speaks out about the case, the lack of evidence and the abuse of power by Phiyega, Abrahams and Jiba - and of course the Sunday Times.

Press Release:


Booysen Exclusive
In an exclusive one-on-one interview Major General Booysen—suspended head of the KZN Hawks—tells his story for the first time. As the alleged boss of the so-called Cato Manor Death Squad, Booysen speaks frankly to Carte Blanche about charges levelled against him, the abuse of state resources, his life in the force and the capture of democratic institutions.


Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: In 2012, the then KZN HAWKS Boss Major General Johan Booysen and 27 members of the Cato Manor Organised Crime Unit were arrested.

An investigation was launched, after a series of photographs were leaked to the press. The Unit was labelled a death squad – and faced 116 charges; they stand accused of the planting of weapons, racketeering and murder.

JOHAN: There is no Death Squad. That’s a figment of someone’s imagination. // INT1 M7 look I am not saying they are angels – none of us are angels – but we are not racketeers, they are not murderers. INT2 M18

VO: Four years later General Booysen – accused of calling the shots - reveals his truth in an explosive book. He breaks rank in his first television interview, since his suspension.

JOHAN: I have not had an opportunity to have my story be told. INT1 M1

VO: Booysen’s story started months before the charges were brought against him and the alleged criminal cops.

Rewind to 2010: Major General Booysen had overseen the investigation into politically connected Durban billionaire and fraud accused Thoshan Panday - who is allegedly behind a R60 million tender scam , police corruption of a further 15 million and linked to a R1.3 million bribery case.

Panday has told Carte Blanche that Booysen was never the investigating officer in any of the cases against him. He added that one of the cases was a ploy by Booysen to cause him embarrassment and there was never evidence of wrongdoing against him, the three cases were either thrown out of court or withdrawn. He has denied all the allegations.

But Booysen believed there was evidence that gave cause for concern.

JOHAN: When the investigations that landed on my table commenced – although I felt it was an uncomfortable situation – but I was not going to turn a blind eye.

VO: But before the investigations could be finalised, despite video, documentary and cellphone evidence – Booysen would be arrested, charged and suspended – actions he believes are linked to the Panday investigations.

Panday has been known to brag about his contacts - this leaked undercover video is from 2012. .

PANDAY: Booysen is going maybe next week it's about time
PANDAY: Gone are the days where they think they are controlling everything, they controlling fuck all.

LINK: Being a cop is in his blood // as head of the KZN Hawks - Major General Booysen was not about to give up his dream career because he had seemingly fallen out of favour for trying to expose corruption.

JOHAN: I am fighting criminality within the criminal justice system because the people we are investigating as far as I am concerned are part of a criminal enterprise.

VO: Professor Ivor Chipkin from the Public Affairs Research Institute says this is a long-term trend. HE says there’s a deliberate move to bring autonomous organisations under political control.

CHIPKIN: There is an attempt to remove these people, because they are involved in politically sensitive cases, but they are doing their jobs successfully – so there aren’t any ground to remove to them. Suddenly there is an allegation, that comes through one of these dossiers, they get printed in the newspaper.

VO: The shocking images splashed across newspapers brought back reminders of the tactics of an Apartheid police force many would rather forget.

JOHAN: Let me tell you Devi, there is absolutely nothing wrong with those pictures, the average policeman sees that everyday – those pictures are normal crime scene photographs
DEVI: Those pictures looked bad Johan, they looked bad
JOHAN: Devi, the most dramatic photograph, showing 5 people lying deceased on the back of an LDV they were never shot by Cato Manor.

VO: The armed robbers were killed by members of the Durban Flying Squad, the Dog Unit and Durban Metro Police following an armed robbery in broad daylight.

DEVI: If your guys were doing such a good job – why was this image painted in the media?
JOHAN: I think you have to look at how this whole thing came about – if you look at what subsequently unfolded with factions within Crime Intelligence – with certain journalists and then with people with nefarious agendas – they had to protect their own interest.

LINK: But Major General Booysen’s story is a microcosm of a much bigger challenge facing South Africa – the abuse of state resources and the capture of democratic institutions.

VO: Advocate Nazeer Cassim has chaired and litigated a number of government labour cases - including Major General Booysen’s internal disciplinary hearing – he spoke to us in March.

CASSIM: Government employees, when they are perceived not to be serving the interest of the government, and the government uses what ever arsenal they have available. I don’t think General Booysen is the exception, he may well be the pattern that is followed in government circles if you read the newspapers.

VO: So far, the state has spent over R40 million of tax payers money – on Cato Manor Suspended Cops salaries and legal action against them – but General Booysen believes the greater loss lies in wasted skills.

JOHAN: The suspects that are running the streets now would have been behind bars had Cato Manor still been there – and that’s why I say the people responsible for neutralising Cato Manor – they are the ones with blood on their hands.
DEVI: The damage had been done
CHIPKIN: And we’re talking not just damage to reputation of individuals, we’re talking serious damage to key state institutions
DEVI: Because this playing with fire.
CHIPKIN: this playing with the integrity of South Africa State

VO: But Booysen’s resolve to clear his name, paid off in February 2014, when the racketeering charges against him were set aside. Judge Trevor Gorven was critical of then Acting national director of public prosecutions Nomgcobo Jiba’s original decision to prosecute Booysen.

"Even accepting the least stringent test for rationality imaginable, the decision of the NDPP does not pass muster.”

DEVI: What about your accusers, you called them the Witnesses that Weren’t – are you implying that the witnesses weren’t strong enough – what are you saying?
JOHAN: There are no witnesses that can confirm that there was a death squad. If you look at the docket itself, you are sitting with one witness, a Greek national, who fled the country.

VO: The Greek National was a former police reservist; he was believed to be a key witness, despite leaving South Africa prior to the shootings covered in the indictment against the Cato Manor Unit.

JOHAN: Sitting with a second witness, Colonel Rajen Aiyer – who has been discredited in the regional court in Durban, he’s been discredited during my disciplinary hearing where he has been found to a dismal and a dishonest witness – and in any event, even if what he says in his statement is true, it doesn’t amount to racketeering – it’s office politics.

VO: We have in our possession snippets of a phone conversation between Colonel Aiyer and a colleague – it seems the Colonel has never been a fan of General Booysen.

AIYER: Director Johan Booysen. That is the thorn in our flesh. I want him out!
COLLEAGUE: Do you want him out?
AIYER: I want him out - OUT! OUT! OUT! OUT!

JOHAN: And then you are sitting with a third person that is a deceased person, who’s evidence is hearsay is twice removed

VO: With the racketeering charges out of the way, Booysen was then cleared in an internal disciplinary hearing chaired by Advocate Nazeer Cassim in September 2014.

He returned to work – despite being offered his full pension payout, three years additional salary and a full tax rebate if he left quietly.

DEVI: Why did you not take the golden handshake?
JOHAN: At the time it was unfinished business. I knew I wanted to go back, which I did. Much to the dismay of General Phiyega at the time – the very first thing I did after I returned back to office was to continue with this investigation that I knew had basically become dormant. I wasn’t going to back off. To me it would have been capitulating and I wasn’t going to do that.

VO: He escalated the cases to the Independent Police INVESTIGATIVE Directorate - the then IPID boss Robert McBride reviewed the dockets.

UPSOUND MCBRIDE
MCBRIDE: There’s clearly a prosecutable case against Thoshan Panday
DEVI: Clear! Clear! Clear!
MCBRIDE: Water tight.

VO: Part of the evidence is an independent forensic audit that the police commissioned.

The audit report found fraud – revealing inappropriate relationships between Panday and key police figures. KZN Provincial Commissioner Mmamonnye Ngobeni is one of the officials said to have benefited.
Panday allegedly paid for Ngobeni’s husband’s surprise birthday party.
MCBRIDE: He paid with his own credit card…
VO: The Commissioner maintains her innocence, insisting that she had used Panday to plan the party and that she had paid him for it.
Commisioner Ngobeni was suspended in May, and is challenging it.
McBride’s investigation into the matter did not go unnoticed.
JOHAN: He actually predicted to me that he would suspended and I said to him, there’s no way they will suspend you – and the rest is history.

VO: Booysen’s return to office would be short lived – the racketeering charges would be reinstated a year later.

DEVI: Why do you think the NPA comes back over and over again reinstating charges?
JOHAN: If I had not gone back to work and revisited these charges. I honestly believe if I had taken the golden handshake at the time these charges would not have been reinstituted.

VO: Finally last week, it would appear that his efforts are starting to pay off.
In this official 2011 police sting video, Thoshan Panday’s co-accused, Col Navin Madhoe, is seen placing a suitcase said to contain R1-point-three million in cash, into Booysen’s boot - allegedly in exchange for help to make the original case go away.
Col Madhoe has declined to comment, and while Panday has denied any involvement, the National Director of Public Prosecutions Shaun Abrahams decided to prosecute both men in relation to the Booysen bribery case.
Booysen feels the wheels of justice are turning but says the matter is far from over.

JOHAN: This whole matter is sub judice and I think lets grant Mr. Panday and Colonel Madhoe the opportunity – and in terms of our constitution they are innocent until proven guilty – // it’s up to the courts to decide. INT2 M17

LINK: Major General Booysen is currently suspended – he has been to court 6 times challenging the charges against him – winning, every time, with costs – yet he has not been allowed to return to work.

CASSIM: It is a sad reality of South Africa, that here is policeman, passionate about his job, tremendous work record, highly recommended by Judges and a number of other people and what he wants to do is his job and what the government wants to do is just suspend him and keep him away from his job and his job is to deal with law and order which is a menace that every South African feels on a daily basis.

CHIPKIN: What would have happened if all of those people were still in their positions, in other words, if they haven’t been removed. One has to wonder how far would those investigation been had those cases had those people still been in place.

VO: Just 10 months from retirement – Booysen realises, he probably won’t get back to office.

DEVI: Do you feel robbed though?
JOHAN: //I feel robbed in that I know in the twilight of my career I could have made a huge difference especially to violent crime and organised crime in the province and that opportunity has been taken away from me. INT2 M21
JOHAN: if you were to ask me if I had to chose again – would I take the same decision that I took four years ago – I’ll take the same decision COMMENTBACK TO FRONT - INT2 M20
DEVI: No Regrets?
JOHAN: No Regrets

 

PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: KZN Hawks Boss General Booysen – reveals his truth for the first since his suspension.

JOHAN: There is no Death Squad. That’s a figment of someone’s imagination.

PROMO 2
VO: We bring you an exclusive interview with Suspended KZN Hawks Boss Major General Johan Booysen.

JOHAN: I honestly believe if I had taken the golden handshake at the time these charges would not have been reinstituted.

PROMO 3
VO: Suspended KZN Hawks Boss Major General Johan Booysen speaks out about the charges levelled against him and the alleged death squad.

JOHAN: The people responsible for neutralising Cato Manor – they are the ones with blood on their hands. INT1 M6

VO: Booysen’s return to office would be short lived – the racketeering charges would be reinstated a year later. DEVI: Why do you think the NPA comes back over and over again reinstating charges? JOHAN: If I had not gone back to work and revisited these charges. I honestly believe if I had taken the golden handshake at the time these charges would not have been reinstituted. VO: Finally last week, it would appear that his efforts are starting to pay off. In this official 2011 police sting video, Thoshan Panday’s co-accused, Col Navin Madhoe, is seen placing a suitcase said to contain R1-point-three million in cash, into Booysen’s boot - allegedly in exchange for help to make the original case go away. Col Madhoe has declined to comment, and while Panday has denied any involvement, the National Director of Public Prosecutions Shaun Abrahams decided to prosecute both men in relation to the Booysen bribery case. Booysen feels the wheels of justice are turning but says the matter is far from over. JOHAN: This whole matter is sub judice and I think lets grant Mr. Panday and Colonel Madhoe the opportunity – and in terms of our constitution they are innocent until proven guilty – // it’s up to the courts to decide. INT2 M17 LINK: Major General Booysen is currently suspended – he has been to court 6 times challenging the charges against him – winning, every time, with costs – yet he has not been allowed to return to work. CASSIM: It is a sad reality of South Africa, that here is policeman, passionate about his job, tremendous work record, highly recommended by Judges and a number of other people and what he wants to do is his job and what the government wants to do is just suspend him and keep him away from his job and his job is to deal with law and order which is a menace that every South African feels on a daily basis. CHIPKIN: What would have happened if all of those people were still in their positions, in other words, if they haven’t been removed. One has to wonder how far would those investigation been had those cases had those people still been in place. VO: Just 10 months from retirement – Booysen realises, he probably won’t get back to office. DEVI: Do you feel robbed though? JOHAN: //I feel robbed in that I know in the twilight of my career I could have made a huge difference especially to violent crime and organised crime in the province and that opportunity has been taken away from me. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): General Mayor Booysen, suspended head of the KZN HAWKS and alleged boss behind the Cato Manor Death Squad speaks out for the first time in his first television interview.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: WE EXCLUSIVELY GET THE FIRST SIT DOWN INTERVIEW WITH MAJOR GENERAL JOHAN BOOYSEN! In the four years since his suspension - he has not granted any interviews.
metadata.Summary: In December 2011, 28 members of the Cato Manor Organised Crime Unit were arrested and accused of operating like death-squad - eight months later Major General Johan Booysen was also suspended and tipped as the man allegedly behind the unit's alleged killing spree. We sit down and get the full story from Major General Booysen.
metadata.Further information: Suspended KZN HAWKS Boss, Major General Johan Booysen, has had racketeering charges re-instated against him, he has beaten the NPA in court 6 times previously - he has won all the cases with costs – that means it has cost the State in excess of R2 million to take him on and lose. Further more they have spent an additional R1.7 million rand on a disciplinary hearing against Booysen – where the independent external Senior Advocate Cassim also found in favour of Booysen. After winning all his cases, Booysen was offered a golden handsake to retire by Phiyega – I have the specifics details – he declined the offer and chose to take up his position after being cleared yet again only to be charged again. While on suspension the HAWKS have permanently appointed a new KZN HAWKS Boss – the police are essentially paying two salaries for the job at the moment. For the first time in a sit down interview Booysen speaks out about the case, the lack of evidence and the abuse of power by Phiyega, Abrahams and Jiba - and of course the Sunday Times.
